parts.label: the diagnosis
turns: Priya Raman (Partner, Calder Lane Advisory): Let's close out the Harrow & Finch Grocers engagement. Their CFO Dana Whitlock signed off yesterday.

Tom Okafor (Associate, Calder Lane Advisory): The headline: Harrow & Finch's net margin fell from 4.1% to 2.7% over two years, and it was not price competition. 61% of the erosion came from shrink and markdowns on fresh produce in the 38 Leeds-area stores.

Priya Raman (Partner, Calder Lane Advisory): Right. The pattern I want us to keep: when a grocer's margin drops and everyone blames discounters, check fresh shrink before pricing. Category-level shrink was the real driver.

Tom Okafor (Associate, Calder Lane Advisory): The framework that worked was the three-lens margin bridge: price/mix, shrink, and labour-per-case, each measured per store cluster rather than per store.

parts.label: getting it approved
turns: Priya Raman (Partner, Calder Lane Advisory): Also: Dana's team rejected the first recommendation because it cut staff. Reframing the same savings as ordering-cadence changes got it approved within a week.
Tom Okafor (Associate, Calder Lane Advisory): Noted. Lesson: in family-owned grocers, recommendations that touch headcount stall; ordering and replenishment fixes get approved fast.
Priya Raman (Partner, Calder Lane Advisory): And their head of stores, Graham Pike, only engaged once we showed the store-cluster results on a single page. The 40-slide deck went unread.
Tom Okafor (Associate, Calder Lane Advisory): So for operations leaders: lead with a one-page cluster view and keep the detailed deck as backup.

shortcut.why: Tom, starting the next grocer engagement, wants the number handy and pins it straight into the library
shortcut.text: Benchmark from Harrow & Finch: fresh shrink and markdowns were 61% of their margin erosion.

questions.q: A regional grocer's margin is falling and the CEO blames discount chains. Where should we look first?
How do we get cost-saving recommendations approved at a family-owned grocer?
How should we present findings to a head of stores?
